target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (X Y : Type) (P : S2 X Y) (T : ℕ),
    ∃ N : S1 X Y, N.D9 ∧ N.d13 = T ∧
      ∀ xs : List X, xs.length ≤ T → N.d4 xs = P.d4 xs
a_raw: {"translation":"Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every type X, every type Y, every P of type S2 X Y, and every natural number T, there exists a single N of type S1 X Y with all three properties: (1) Its dependency graph has no cycle, including a self-loop: no node has a path of one or more edges back to itself. There is an edge from m to n exactly when there exist two full state assignments agreeing at every node other than m and an input x for which the updates at n from those assignments differ. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. (2) N has exactly T nodes, not merely at most T; this counts nodes, not the values their states can take. (3) For every finite list xs of elements of X of length at most T, the final outputs of N and P on xs are equal. Both start from their respective initial states and process xs from left to right: N updates all nodes from the previous assignment and reads out the final assignment, while P updates both components from the previous pair and reads out only the final second component. N may depend on X, Y, P, and T but must work for all such lists, including the empty list. No agreement of internal states or of outputs on longer lists is required. T may be zero, in which case N must have no nodes and output agreement is required only on the empty list."}
translation: Target defines, but does not prove, the following proposition. For every type X, every type Y, every P of type S2 X Y, and every natural number T, there exists a single N of type S1 X Y with all three properties: (1) Its dependency graph has no cycle, including a self-loop: no node has a path of one or more edges back to itself. There is an edge from m to n exactly when there exist two full state assignments agreeing at every node other than m and an input x for which the updates at n from those assignments differ. The assignments need not be reachable from the initial state. (2) N has exactly T nodes, not merely at most T; this counts nodes, not the values their states can take. (3) For every finite list xs of elements of X of length at most T, the final outputs of N and P on xs are equal. Both start from their respective initial states and process xs from left to right: N updates all nodes from the previous assignment and reads out the final assignment, while P updates both components from the previous pair and reads out only the final second component. N may depend on X, Y, P, and T but must work for all such lists, including the empty list. No agreement of internal states or of outputs on longer lists is required. T may be zero, in which case N must have no nodes and output agreement is required only on the empty list.

divergences.description: The claim that the class includes every system with plasticity goes beyond the TARGET. It quantifies only over `S2 X Y`: systems with a fixed initial pair, deterministic updates of both components at each input step, and a readout from the second component. The first component can represent changing weights, but Lean neither defines plasticity in general nor states that every plastic system has such a representation.

judgement.summary: Within `S2`, the description is accurate: one acyclic system with exactly T units must match outputs on all histories of length at most T. The passage report is also accurate and distinguishes the paper’s claim of breakdown after t0 from the TARGET’s different test of equivalence.
